# Rhosyn Dunkford

Rhosyn Dunkford is the founder and CEO of Zorrel Analytics, a maritime technology company specializing in advanced software for port terminal operations. With over 18 years of experience in logistics technology and maritime systems integration, Dunkford has been a pivotal figure in modernizing berth scheduling and container management workflows.

The flagship product Dunkford developed under Zorrel Analytics is DockFlow, an advanced berth scheduling software that predicts optimal vessel docking times to maximize terminal throughput and minimize vessel waiting periods. DockFlow integrates real-time crane telemetry, vessel position data, and customs clearance processes to deliver a comprehensive scheduling solution tailored for complex, multi-berth terminals.

Dunkford conceived the idea for DockFlow during her tenure as a systems engineer at a major port operator from 2006 to 2013. She identified that existing berth scheduling relied heavily on manual spreadsheets and static rules, which often led to inefficient usage of berths and costly delays. Using her background in operations research and predictive modeling, Dunkford began prototyping algorithms that could dynamically adjust berth assignments based on live data feeds and predictive analytics. 

In 2014, Dunkford founded Zorrel Analytics with an initial team of five engineers. The company’s early pilot deployments of DockFlow were with the Port of Lancorrin and the Eastshore Terminal Consortium, both critical hubs with complex vessel traffic patterns. These initial customers reported a 12-18% reduction in average vessel waiting times within the first six months of using DockFlow. Feedback from these pilots led to rapid iteration and incorporation of features such as berth conflict resolution alerts and integration with customs clearance workflows.

DockFlow employs a proprietary predictive engine that evaluates factors including vessel ETA variability, crane availability, and customs clearance windows. It then simulates multiple scheduling scenarios to recommend the optimal docking sequence that maximizes berth utilization and minimizes idle crane time. The software’s dashboard provides terminal operators with real-time visibility and adjustment controls, allowing manual overrides when necessary.

Regarding pricing, Zorrel Analytics experimented through 2017-2019 with both license-based and subscription models. After extensive market research and customer feedback, DockFlow is now offered primarily as a SaaS subscription with tiered plans based on terminal size and throughput volume. Entry-level plans start at $8,000 per month for terminals handling up to 50 vessel calls, while large-scale enterprise licenses for terminals with over 200 vessel calls run upwards of $45,000 monthly.

The DockFlow roadmap under Dunkford’s guidance includes expanded machine learning capabilities to predict customs clearance delays, enhanced integration with crane telemetry systems for fine-grained scheduling, and a mobile interface for terminal supervisors. Planned future releases will also incorporate blockchain-based container tracking modules to further streamline container handoffs and clearance.

Rhosyn Dunkford remains actively involved in product design and strategic partnerships, steering DockFlow’s evolution as a transformational tool in maritime terminal operations worldwide. Her blend of technical expertise and frontline maritime operations insight continues to shape Zorrel Analytics’ growth and innovation trajectory.
